<style>
  .page {
    max-width: var(--lc-page-width);
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 0 var(--lc-space-3);
  }

  /* -------- Top bar -------- */
  .topbar {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    padding: var(--lc-space-3) 0;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .topbar .mark {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--lc-space-1);
    color: var(--lc-text);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-display);
    font-weight: 700;
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xl);
    letter-spacing: -0.01em;
    text-decoration: none;
  }
  .topbar .mark img {
    width: 36px;
    height: 36px;
    object-fit: contain;
  }
  .topbar .meta-links {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
  }
  .topbar .meta-links a {
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    text-decoration: none;
  }
  .topbar .meta-links a:hover { color: var(--lc-text); }
  .topbar .star-btn {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 6px;
    border: 1px solid var(--lc-text);
    color: var(--lc-text);
    background: var(--lc-card-bg);
    padding: 6px 12px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    font-family: var(--lc-font-body);
    text-decoration: none;
  }
  .topbar .star-btn:hover { background: var(--lc-text); color: var(--lc-background); }
  .topbar .star-btn strong {
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-yellow) 30%, transparent);
    padding: 0 6px;
    border-radius: 4px;
  }

  /* -------- Hero -------- */
  .hero {
    padding-top: var(--lc-space-6);
    padding-bottom: var(--lc-space-8);
    position: relative;
  }
  .hero-grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1.05fr 1fr;
    gap: var(--lc-space-6);
    align-items: center;
  }
  .hero-left .eyebrow {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-loom-wood);
    letter-spacing: 0.08em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--lc-space-1);
  }
  .hero-left .eyebrow::before {
    content: "";
    display: inline-block;
    width: 32px; height: 2px;
    background: var(--lc-loom-wood);
  }
  .hero-wordmark {
    width: min(540px, 100%);
    height: auto;
    mix-blend-mode: multiply;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .hero h1 {
    font-size: clamp(40px, 5vw, 56px);
    font-weight: 700;
    color: var(--lc-text);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .hero h1 .accent {
    color: var(--lc-loom-wood);
    font-style: italic;
    font-weight: 700;
  }
  .hero .subhead {
    font-size: var(--lc-text-lg);
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    max-width: 52ch;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-4);
  }
  .hero .ctas {
    display: flex;
    gap: var(--lc-space-2);
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .hero .status-line {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: var(--lc-space-2);
    align-items: center;
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
  }
  .hero .status-line .sep { color: var(--lc-rule); }
  .hero .status-line .live-dot {
    width: 8px; height: 8px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: var(--lc-agent-green);
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-green) 30%, transparent);
    display: inline-block;
    margin-right: 4px;
  }

  /* Hero illustration - loom ring with agents */
  .hero-art {
    position: relative;
    aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
    width: 100%;
    max-width: 480px;
    margin-left: auto;
    justify-self: end;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
  }
  .hero-art .hero-logo {
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    object-fit: contain;
  }

  /* -------- Status banner -------- */
  .status-banner {
    background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-green) 14%, var(--lc-background));
    border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-green) 40%, transparent);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius);
    padding: var(--lc-space-3) var(--lc-space-4);
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-8);
  }
  .status-banner .leaf {
    font-size: 28px;
    line-height: 1;
    flex-shrink: 0;
  }
  .status-banner h3 {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-body);
    font-weight: 600;
    font-size: var(--lc-text-base);
    margin-bottom: 2px;
  }
  .status-banner p {
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
  }

  /* -------- Section scaffolding -------- */
  .section {
    padding: var(--lc-space-8) 0;
    border-top: 1px dashed var(--lc-rule);
    position: relative;
  }
  .section:first-of-type { border-top: 0; padding-top: 0; }
  .section-head {
    display: flex;
    align-items: baseline;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-4);
    flex-wrap: wrap;
  }
  .section-head .num {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-loom-wood);
    letter-spacing: 0.08em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
  }
  .section h2 {
    font-size: clamp(28px, 3.5vw, 40px);
    font-weight: 700;
    color: var(--lc-text);
    max-width: 22ch;
    flex: 1 1 auto;
  }
  .section .lede {
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-lg);
    max-width: 64ch;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-4);
  }

  /* -------- Primitives grid -------- */
  .primitives-grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .primitives-grid > article:first-child,
  .primitives-grid > article:nth-child(2) { grid-column: span 1; }
  .primitives-grid > article:nth-child(5) { grid-column: span 2; }
  .primitive {
    position: relative;
    border: 1px solid var(--lc-rule);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-lg);
    background: var(--lc-card-bg);
    padding: var(--lc-space-4);
    overflow: hidden;
    box-shadow: var(--lc-shadow-sm);
    transition: transform 200ms ease, box-shadow 200ms ease;
  }
  .primitive:hover {
    transform: translateY(-2px);
    box-shadow: var(--lc-shadow);
  }
  .primitive .accent {
    position: absolute;
    top: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
    height: 4px;
  }
  .primitive .agent-pop {
    width: 100px;
    height: 100px;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);
  }
  /* Mascot videos - autoplay-loop characters that replace the prior chibi-SVG slots */
  .mascot-video {
    object-fit: contain;
    display: block;
    background: transparent;
    /* Source videos are 400×400 yuv420p (no alpha); the cream-ish background blends with the page bg */
  }
  .primitive .primitive-name {
    display: flex;
    align-items: baseline;
    gap: var(--lc-space-2);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-1);
  }
  .primitive h3 {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-display);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xl);
    font-weight: 700;
    letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  }
  .primitive .shipped {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xs);
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    padding: 2px 8px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-yellow) 30%, transparent);
    border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-agent-yellow) 50%, transparent);
  }
  .primitive p {
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);
    line-height: 1.6;
  }
  .primitive pre {
    margin: 0;
    background: var(--lc-code-bg);
    color: var(--lc-code-text);
    padding: var(--lc-space-2);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-sm);
    font-size: 12px;
    line-height: 1.5;
    overflow-x: auto;
  }
  .primitive pre .k { color: var(--lc-agent-orange); }
  .primitive pre .s { color: var(--lc-agent-green); }
  .primitive pre .c { color: #8C8FA3; font-style: italic; }

  /* -------- Trust model -------- */
  .trust-grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
    gap: 0;
    border: 1.5px solid var(--lc-text);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-lg);
    overflow: hidden;
    background: var(--lc-card-bg);
  }
  .trust-col {
    padding: var(--lc-space-4);
  }
  .trust-col + .trust-col { border-left: 1.5px solid var(--lc-text); }
  .trust-col .label {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xs);
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.1em;
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-1);
  }
  .trust-col h3 {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-display);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xl);
    font-weight: 700;
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .trust-col ul {
    margin: 0 0 var(--lc-space-3) 0;
    padding: 0;
    list-style: none;
  }
  .trust-col li {
    padding: var(--lc-space-1) 0;
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-text);
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 18px 1fr;
    gap: var(--lc-space-1);
    line-height: 1.5;
  }
  .trust-col li::before {
    content: "•";
    color: var(--lc-loom-wood);
  }
  .trust-col .when {
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-text-muted);
    border-top: 1px dashed var(--lc-rule);
    padding-top: var(--lc-space-2);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-body);
    line-height: 1.5;
  }
  .trust-col.deny h3 { color: #B83232; }
  .trust-col.allow h3 { color: var(--lc-loom-wood); }
  .trust-footer {
    margin-top: var(--lc-space-3);
    padding: var(--lc-space-3);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-base);
    color: var(--lc-text);
    background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-thread-purple) 8%, var(--lc-background));
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius);
    border-left: 4px solid var(--lc-thread-purple);
  }
  .trust-footer strong { color: var(--lc-thread-purple); }

  /* -------- Providers -------- */
  .providers-wrap {
    background: var(--lc-code-bg);
    color: var(--lc-code-text);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-lg);
    padding: var(--lc-space-4) var(--lc-space-6);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-base);
    line-height: 1.7;
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  .providers-wrap::before {
    content: "// six providers, one interface";
    position: absolute;
    top: 12px;
    right: 16px;
    font-size: var(--lc-text-xs);
    color: #6B6F87;
    opacity: 0.7;
  }
  .providers-flow {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 220px auto 280px;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
    align-items: center;
  }
  .providers-flow .list {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 6px;
  }
  .providers-flow .list .p {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--lc-space-2);
  }
  .providers-flow .p .dot {
    width: 8px; height: 8px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    flex-shrink: 0;
  }
  .providers-flow .p span { color: var(--lc-code-text); }
  .providers-flow .arrows svg {
    width: 80px; height: 200px;
  }
  .providers-flow .interface {
    border: 1px solid #4A4D60;
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius);
    padding: var(--lc-space-3);
    background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04);
  }
  .providers-flow .interface h4 {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: var(--lc-agent-yellow);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);
    font-weight: 500;
  }
  .providers-flow .interface .row {
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: #C8CBDD;
    padding: 4px 0;
    border-top: 1px dashed #3A3D52;
  }
  .providers-flow .interface .row:first-of-type { border-top: 0; }
  .providers-flow .interface .row .k {
    color: var(--lc-agent-orange);
    margin-right: 8px;
  }
  .providers-foot {
    margin-top: var(--lc-space-3);
    padding-top: var(--lc-space-2);
    border-top: 1px dashed #3A3D52;
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    color: #C8CBDD;
  }
  .providers-foot .key {
    color: var(--lc-agent-green);
  }

  /* -------- War story -------- */
  .war-story {
    border-left: 4px solid var(--lc-loom-wood);
    padding-left: var(--lc-space-4);
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 140px 1fr;
    gap: var(--lc-space-4);
    align-items: start;
  }
  .war-story .agent-anchor {
    width: 140px;
  }
  .war-story h2 {
    font-size: var(--lc-text-3xl);
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);
  }
  .war-story .body p {
    margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);
    color: var(--lc-text);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-base);
    line-height: 1.65;
    max-width: 64ch;
  }
  .war-story .body p strong { color: var(--lc-text); }
  .war-story .body .punch {
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius);
    background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-loom-wood) 10%, var(--lc-background));
    padding: var(--lc-space-3);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--lc-loom-wood);
    margin-top: var(--lc-space-2);
  }
  .war-story .read-more {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 6px;
    margin-top: var(--lc-space-3);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-body);
    font-weight: 600;
    text-decoration: none;
    color: var(--lc-thread-purple);
  }
  .war-story .read-more:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

  /* -------- Quickstart -------- */
  .quickstart-block {
    background: var(--lc-code-bg);
    color: var(--lc-code-text);
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-lg);
    padding: var(--lc-space-4) var(--lc-space-4);
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);
    line-height: 1.8;
    overflow-x: auto;
    position: relative;
  }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar {
    position: absolute;
    top: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
    height: 32px;
    background: #0F0F1F;
    border-radius: var(--lc-radius-lg) var(--lc-radius-lg) 0 0;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    padding: 0 12px;
    gap: 6px;
  }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar i {
    width: 10px; height: 10px;
    border-radius: 50%;
  }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar i:nth-child(1) { background: #FF5F57; }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar i:nth-child(2) { background: #FEBC2E; }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar i:nth-child(3) { background: #28C840; }
  .quickstart-block .titlebar .name {
    margin-left: var(--lc-space-2);
    font-size: 11px;
    color: #8C8FA3;
  }
  .quickstart-block .body { padding-top: var(--lc-space-4); white-space: pre-wrap; }
  .quickstart-block .prompt { color: var(--lc-agent-teal); }
  .quickstart-block .comment { color: #8C8FA3; font-style: italic; }
  .quickstart-block .ok { color: var(--lc-agent-green); }
  .quickstart-block .str { color: var(--lc-agent-orange); }
  .quickstart-block .heading {
    color: #6B6F87;
    font-size: 11px;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.1em;
    margin: var(--lc-space-2) 0 var(--lc-space-1) 0;
  }

  /* -------- Roadmap -------- */
  .roadmap {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    gap: var(--lc-space-2);
  }
  .roadmap-item {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 130px 1fr;
    gap: var(--lc-space-3);
    padding: var(--lc-space-3) 0;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--lc-rule);
    align-items: start;
  }
  .roadmap-item:first-child { border-top: 0; }
  .roadmap-item .v {
    font-family: var(--lc-font-mono);
    font-size: var(--lc-text-base);
    font-weight: 700;
    color: var(--lc-text);
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 6px;
  }
  .roadmap-item .v .badge {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;

  <section class="section" id="why">
    <div class="section-head">
      <span class="num">§ 03 - why this exists</span>
      <h2>Ten things that are uncommon, together.</h2>
    </div>
    <p class="lede">Most agent platforms pick one of three shapes - a library you embed, a hosted service you rent, or a gateway that doesn't run the loop. loomcycle is something different: a self-hostable runtime that owns the loop, speaks every wire surface (HTTP, gRPC, MCP, TS adapter, Python adapter), and stays out of your application's process.</p>

    <div class="why-grid">
      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">01</span>
        <h3>Self-contained Go binary, ~50 MB.</h3>
        <p>No Node, no Python, no JVM in the model path. Drop it in alongside your application and forget it's there.</p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">02</span>
        <h3>The runtime runs outside your app process.</h3>
        <p>Sidecar wire surfaces: HTTP, gRPC, MCP, TypeScript adapter (<code>@loomcycle/client</code>), Python adapter (<code>loomcycle</code> on PyPi). Your application stays in whatever language you wrote it in.</p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">03</span>
        <h3>MCP client <em>and</em> MCP server, simultaneously.</h3>
        <p>Agents you host are reachable from outside as MCP tools; tools outside are mountable inside as MCP servers. Most products are one side of the protocol; loomcycle is both.</p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">04</span>
        <h3>External MCP fan-out - one call, N concurrent runs.</h3>
        <p><code>spawn_runs(mode: "join", spawns: […])</code> dispatches N agent runs concurrently from one MCP call and returns an index-aligned envelope when they settle. The shape exp7 used to drive 10 reviewers from one Claude Code call. <a href="/blog/claude-code-as-operator-loomcycle-as-side-runtime.html">exp7 writeup →</a></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">05</span>
        <h3>Security by design - secrets never touch the LLM.</h3>
        <p>Three guarantees the substrate makes:
          <strong>(a)</strong> Per-run credentials are substituted at the MCP transport boundary - agents see credential <em>names</em>, never <em>values</em>; the LLM's view of its credentials map is empty of resolved tokens.
          <strong>(b)</strong> The <code>redact</code> run-loop plugin scrubs operator-declared secrets from every outbound LLM request - <strong>Tier-A</strong>: operator declares env vars whose values get masked exactly (<em>customizable</em> - add more env vars whenever a new secret class appears); <strong>Tier-B</strong>: built-in heuristic patterns catch <code>Authorization</code> headers, <code>sk-…</code> OpenAI keys, <code>ghp_…</code> GitHub tokens, AWS / Slack / generic <code>key=value</code> shapes regardless of operator config.
          <strong>(c)</strong> Value-based redaction-at-rest catches anything that bypassed (a) and (b) - the persisted transcript and snapshot never carry literal tokens, even if an agent inlined one into a Bash command.
          <a href="/blog/scrub-before-the-model-sees-it.html">writeup →</a></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">06</span>
        <h3>Built for long sessions - auto-compaction + pluggable run-loop transforms.</h3>
        <p><strong>Context auto-compaction</strong> (v0.32.0) keeps long-running agentic sessions in budget - three coordinated triggers around one shared summarizer: <em>manual</em> (operator clicks Compact), <em>auto</em> (per-iteration threshold crosses <code>autocompact_at_pct</code>), <em>self</em> (agent calls <code>Context op=compact</code> itself). Keeps the pinned task + summary + last-N; snaps the cut to a clean user-turn boundary so a <code>tool_use</code>/<code>tool_results</code> pair is never split.
          The <code>contextplugin</code> chain runs every iteration between agent and LLM - <code>redact</code> (above) is the first built-in; <strong>a context-compressor plugin is the next built-in coming</strong>, moving compaction logic into the same operator-customizable surface. Plugins live in the loop, not the agent.
          <a href="/blog/context-compaction-for-long-running-agents.html">writeup →</a></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">07</span>
        <h3>Code-as-agent AND LLM-agent in the same loop.</h3>
        <p><code>provider: code-js</code> runs operator-authored JavaScript via <a href="https://github.com/dop251/goja">goja</a> - no host filesystem needed. Same AgentDef shape, same scoping rules, same sub-agent composition. Code agents can spawn LLM agents and vice versa. <a href="/blog/code-agents-without-a-host-filesystem.html">writeup →</a></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">08</span>
        <h3>Production shape - multi-replica HA, pause/snapshot anytime, 8-hour soak.</h3>
        <p>Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY backplane. Pause/snapshot anytime, even mid-run; restore on a different instance - exp6.5 wipes a DB and the paused breeder finishes its work autonomously on the fresh box. <strong>8-hour stability soak: 1.27M circuits, 3.8M agent runs, 100% completion across 468 waves, zero leaks.</strong> <a href="/blog/reliable-under-stress-sustainable-for-hours.html">writeup →</a></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">09</span>
        <h3>Encrypted per-tenant secrets (CredentialDef).</h3>
        <p>Envelope AES-256-GCM. A deployment KEK (<code>LOOMCYCLE_SECRET_KEY</code>) plus a per-tenant DEK derived via HKDF-SHA256. GCM AAD binds each ciphertext to <code>(key_id, tenant, scope, scope_id, name)</code>, so a row copied to another tenant fails authentication at decrypt. <code>$cred:</code> substitution in HTTP MCP headers resolves per-request from the run's identity (agent > user > tenant). A CredentialDef named <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code> at tenant scope shadows the operator host key for every Anthropic call from that tenant's runs. Same shape for OpenAI / Gemini / DeepSeek / Ollama / Brave. Rotation via current + previous KEK; lazy re-encrypt on read. Snapshots exclude sealed rows by design. <strong>Shipped v1.11.0 · RFC AR.</strong></p>
      </article>

      <article class="why-item">
        <span class="why-num">10</span>
        <h3>Enforceable per-scope token + cost budgets.</h3>
        <p>Set a monthly cap; the runtime refuses new runs at admission when it would cross the ceiling (429 on HTTP, <code>ResourceExhausted</code> on gRPC). Most-restrictive-of-operator/tenant/user wins. Soft-warn threshold fires an Interruption; hard-cap denies. A new <code>EventLimit</code> event rides the same channel as text / tool-use / thinking events, on HTTP SSE + gRPC + MCP + TS adapter + Python adapter + the Web UI's run terminal (amber banner soft, red hard, inline in the transcript). The in-memory tracker boot-seeds from the token_usage ledger, so a restart doesn't reset counters. A Web UI Limits page renders the live month-to-date used column with K/M/G shorthand. <strong>Shipped v1.11.0 · RFC AW.</strong></p>
      </article>
    </div>

      <div class="angle-body angle-body-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="angle-1">
        <h3>Sidecar - for engineers building agentic SaaS without adopting a framework.</h3>
        <p class="lede">You're shipping a product whose agents need to run at scale, in parallel, under multi-tenant constraints, with audit and observability - and you don't want to make your application <em>become</em> an agent framework to do it. loomcycle is the runtime your services talk to over HTTP / gRPC / MCP; your application stays in whatever language you wrote it.</p>
        <p>The first agentic feature most teams ship is interactive: a user clicks a button, an agent answers, the conversation ends. The second is harder. Agents need to run at 3am whether or not anyone's logged in. They need to react to a GitHub PR opening, a Stripe invoice failing, a Linear issue moving to "In Review." They need to scale to many users without each user starving another. They need OTEL, a packet-capture residency story, and a trust boundary that holds when a secret accidentally lands in a tool call. <strong>None of this is the loop's problem; it's the surrounding substrate's problem</strong> - and loomcycle ships that substrate.</p>
        <p>The substrate primitives - Memory, Channel, AgentDef, Scheduler, Webhook, A2A, Evaluation, Context - emerged from real consumer pain. <strong>JobEmber.ai</strong> (an AI-driven job-search SaaS) is loomcycle's first consumer: its nightly per-user run touches three per-user MCP servers (jobs, Slack, Telegram) without exposing tokens to the agent, fires on a cron schedule per user tier, and survives a long night under multi-replica HA. The 8-hour stability soak that gates this release came from asking that production-load question. It survived: <strong>1.27M circuits, 3.8M agent runs, 100% completion, zero leaks</strong>.</p>
        <p>What you give up: a UI canvas. What you keep: your services in whatever language they were in, plus a runtime that knows how to be agentic for them. <a href="/blog/multi-tenant-authorization-and-the-four-bugs-qa-caught.html">Multi-tenant authorization writeup →</a> · <a href="/blog/3000-agents-in-one-stress-test.html">3000 agents in one stress test →</a> · <a href="/blog/reliable-under-stress-sustainable-for-hours.html">8-hour soak writeup →</a></p>
        <div class="ctas">
          <a class="cta cta--primary" href="https://github.com/denn-gubsky/loomcycle/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md">Read the architecture →</a>
          <a class="cta cta--secondary" href="#quickstart">Quickstart →</a>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="angle-body angle-body-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="angle-2">
        <h3>Claude Code's side runtime - for engineers who already drive their day through Claude Code.</h3>
        <p class="lede">Claude Code stays the operator and the conversation surface. loomcycle is the side runtime where the multi-agent work runs. One MCP call from Claude Code fans 10 reviewer agents across a repo; one more call merges their findings; Claude Code never opens a file. exp7 proved the shape end-to-end on loomcycle's own codebase. Prefer a dedicated chat window instead of driving from Claude Code? <strong><a href="/loomboard/">LoomBoard</a></strong> is a native desktop app that talks to the same runtime.</p>
        <p>The shape: a fresh Claude Code session clones a target repo, synthesizes a reviewer agent + skill from its own <code>.claude/</code> artifacts, runs <code>loomcycle import claude-code --from=.claude --write --skills-dest=$PWD/skills</code> to lift the AgentDef + SkillDef into loomcycle's substrate, then makes <strong>one MCP call</strong>: <code>spawn_runs(N=10, mode=join, spawns=[…])</code>. 10 reviewers run concurrently inside loomcycle, each writing findings to a shared Memory ledger. One more <code>spawn_run</code> wakes a consolidator that merges the ledger. Claude Code reads the consolidated report. Its own context never carries the 86 files of the target repo. <a href="/blog/claude-code-as-operator-loomcycle-as-side-runtime.html">exp7 writeup →</a></p>
        <p>Your existing <code>.claude/agents/*.md</code> and <code>.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md</code> move into the loomcycle substrate without rewriting - the importer maps the YAML frontmatter onto AgentDef fields, copies the skill body into the system prompt at config-load, and registers everything as content-addressed Defs. The reverse direction is the <a href="https://github.com/denn-gubsky/claude-code-plugin-loomcycle"><code>claude-code-plugin-loomcycle</code></a> repo - a drop-in Claude Code marketplace plugin that gives Claude Code one-keystroke surfaces to drive your loomcycle substrate (slash commands, skills, opt-in hooks). <a href="/blog/mcp-tools-as-data-then-claude-code-plugin.html">Claude Code plugin writeup →</a></p>
        <p><strong>The cost angle</strong>: Claude Code burns Claude tokens for the conversation that matters. loomcycle can run the delegated agents on <strong>DeepSeek, Ollama, local Mistral, or any other cheaper provider</strong> the structured-loop work doesn't need Claude for. Same MCP wire surface; the model swap is one AgentDef field. exp7's 10 reviewers ran on Claude OAuth here, but the topology is provider-neutral - and a code-as-agent (<code>provider: code-js</code>) costs zero LLM tokens at all. <a href="/blog/the-80-dollars-i-burned-on-claude-code.html">The $80 I burned on Claude Code →</a></p>
        <div class="ctas">
          <a class="cta cta--primary" href="https://github.com/denn-gubsky/loomcycle/tree/main/examples/exp7-code-review-fanout">Try the exp7 example →</a>
          <a class="cta cta--secondary" href="#quickstart">Quickstart →</a>

      </div>

      <div class="angle-body angle-body-3" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="angle-3">
        <h3>Production-shaped - for teams that need OTEL, multi-tenant, multi-replica, signed boundaries, and a residency story.</h3>
        <p class="lede">Self-hosted by design. Multi-replica HA on Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (no Redis dep in v1.0). Three drop-in OTEL profiles. A2A on both sides. Signed input webhooks. Per-run credentials never reach the agent's view of its credentials map. Value-based redaction-at-rest plus an outbound-scrub plugin chain. Apache-2.0, residency you can prove with a packet capture.</p>
        <p>The boring-but-load-bearing v1.0 message. Whatever stack you're integrating, the trust boundaries hold: <strong>A2A on both sides</strong> (RFC G) - loomcycle publishes an AgentCard at <code>/.well-known/agent-card.json</code> with three protocol bindings (REST, JSON-RPC, gRPC); external A2A peers from Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, and LangGraph deployments call loomcycle agents as remote skills, and loomcycle agents call external A2A peers as synthetic <code>a2a__<peer>__<skill></code> tools. <strong>Signed input webhooks</strong> (RFC H) - HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, two-layer idempotency (in-memory + durable), strict JSONPath payload projection, never silently degrades. <strong>Per-run credentials</strong> (RFC F) - the substrate substitutes resolved secrets at the MCP transport boundary, not in the agent's view of its credentials map. Agents see credential <em>names</em>; the wire sees <em>values</em>; persisted state sees <em>redacted placeholders</em>.</p>
        <p><strong>Two-layer secret discipline</strong>: a <code>redact</code> plugin in the run-loop scrubs secrets before the model sees outbound data; value-based redaction-at-rest catches anything an agent inlined into a tool call so SQLite/Postgres never persist the literal token. The two layers compose - Layer 1 stops secrets reaching the LLM; Layer 2 stops them landing in the DB. An operator's typo (assigning a token to a differently-named shell var) is caught anyway because the match is value-based. <a href="/blog/scrub-before-the-model-sees-it.html">writeup →</a></p>
        <p><strong>Three drop-in OTEL profiles</strong> - self-hosted Grafana/Tempo/Prom/Loki, Honeycomb, Datadog APM. Plus a bearer-authed <code>/metrics</code> Prometheus endpoint live-read from runtime counters. Pick your backend; no vendor SDK in the loop. <strong>Multi-replica HA</strong> on Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (no Redis dep in v1.0); 8-hour stability soak: 1.27M circuits, 3.8M agent runs, 100% completion, zero leaks. <a href="/blog/loomcycle-speaks-a2a.html">A2A writeup →</a> · <a href="/blog/input-webhooks-the-signed-front-door.html">Webhooks writeup →</a> · <a href="/blog/three-mcp-tokens-one-run.html">Per-run credentials writeup →</a></p>

  <!-- =============== WHAT THIS IS NOT =============== -->
  <section class="section" id="what-not">
    <div class="section-head">
      <span class="num">§ 04 - what this is not</span>
      <h2>What loomcycle is not.</h2>
    </div>
    <p class="lede">A short, candid section. If your situation matches any of these, you'll save time by picking a different tool - and we'd rather route you to the right one than waste your day.</p>

    <div class="what-not">
      <p><strong>Not a Python or TypeScript framework you embed.</strong> If you want a library that lives inside your app's process and gives you an agent abstraction at the function-call level, you don't want loomcycle - you want a framework, and there are good ones. loomcycle is the runtime under that framework, or the runtime instead of it.</p>

      <p><strong>Not a no-code builder.</strong> If you want to drag boxes onto a canvas and connect them with arrows, you don't want loomcycle - you want a visual workflow tool. loomcycle plugs into one of those tools as a node provider (the community package is shipped), but loomcycle itself is not the canvas.</p>

      <p><strong>Not a replacement for Claude Code.</strong> If you live in Claude Code, you don't want loomcycle to replace it - you want loomcycle to be where Claude Code delegates the multi-agent work it doesn't want carrying in its own context. exp7 proves the shape: one MCP call, 10 reviewer agents, one consolidator, Claude Code never opened a repo file. <a href="/blog/claude-code-as-operator-loomcycle-as-side-runtime.html">writeup →</a></p>

        <p>Unix-like VFS over Memory, Volumes, and Documents. Tenant-rooted, scope-aware. Borrows the Linux <strong>inode/dirent split</strong>: resources keep permanent ids, a <code>dirents</code> row maps <code>(parent_path, name) → resource</code>. One tree spans three resource kinds; renames are cheap dirent updates that never touch the resource. Six ops (<code>resolve</code> / <code>ls</code> / <code>stat</code> / <code>mkdir</code> / <code>mv</code> / <code>rm</code>). Paths reject <code>..</code>; segments <code>[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+</code>. Resources opt in to a name: <code>Memory.set path:</code>, <code>VolumeDef.create mount_at:</code>, <code>Document.create_document path:</code>. SQL Memory stays out of the tree. A dirent is a <strong>name, not an authority grant</strong> — the resource's own scope/tenant check still applies. On every transport.</p>
<pre><span class="c">// list a directory</span>
{<span class="k">"tool"</span>:<span class="s">"path"</span>,
 <span class="k">"input"</span>:{<span class="k">"op"</span>:<span class="s">"ls"</span>,

Each chunk is a first-class unit: UUID, hierarchy position, optional supertag-like <code>type</code>, structured <code>fields</code>, graph edges, Markdown <code>body</code>, optimistic <code>revision</code>. <strong>Content/structure split</strong>: chunk content lives in Memory keyed by UUID, chunk structure lives in SQL Memory across four tables (<code>documents</code> / <code>chunks</code> / <code>chunk_edges</code> / <code>chunk_types</code>). 13 ops: document lifecycle, chunk CRUD, edges (<code>link_chunks</code> / <code>unlink_chunks</code>), query (structured + <code>under_path</code> Path-join + raw <code>sql:</code> escape hatch through the SQL Memory validator), type defs. Atomic deletes in one SQL Memory transaction; bidirectional edge cleanup; <code>move_chunk</code> cycle guard. A Document at <code>/docs/foo</code> lists as a directory in Path AND resolves as one resource (macOS bundle semantics). On every transport. <strong>v1.5.0:</strong> per-principal <code>/v1/_mcp</code> dispatch (RFC AG) + declared static <code>(tenant, subject)</code> principals (RFC AO) close the cross-transport identity gap, so an agent's MCP-created documents and the Web UI's <code>/ui/paths</code> share the same per-scope SQLite file by construction.</p>

{<span class="k">"tool"</span>:<span class="s">"document"</span>,
 <span class="k">"input"</span>:{<span class="k">"op"</span>:<span class="s">"query_chunks"</span>,

          <h3>CredentialDef</h3>
          <span class="shipped">shipped v1.11.0 · RFC AR</span>
        </div>
        <p>Encrypted per-tenant secret store. Envelope AES-256-GCM: a deployment KEK (<code>LOOMCYCLE_SECRET_KEY</code>) plus a per-tenant DEK derived via HKDF-SHA256. GCM AAD binds each ciphertext to its row identity (<code>key_id | tenant | scope | scope_id | name</code>), so a row copied to another tenant fails authentication at decrypt. Scope precedence <code>agent > user > tenant</code>. Consumers: <code>$cred:<name></code> substitution in HTTP MCPServerDef headers resolves per-request; tenant + user provider-key override by env-var name (a CredentialDef named <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code> at tenant scope shadows the operator host key for every Anthropic call from that tenant). Backends: inline (default) plus stubs for Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager / 1Password Connect. Snapshots exclude sealed rows by design; a restore requires the target deployment to hold equivalent CredentialDefs.</p>
<pre><span class="c">// store a per-tenant API key</span>
{<span class="k">"tool"</span>:<span class="s">"credentialdef"</span>,
 <span class="k">"input"</span>:{<span class="k">"op"</span>:<span class="s">"create"</span>,
         <span class="k">"name"</span>:<span class="s">"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"</span>,
         <span class="k">"scope"</span>:<span class="s">"tenant"</span>,
         <span class="k">"backend"</span>:<span class="s">"inline"</span>,
         <span class="k">"value"</span>:<span class="s">"sk-ant-..."</span>}}</pre>
      </article>

  <!-- =============== TRUST MODEL =============== -->
  <section class="section" id="trust">
    <div class="section-head">
      <span class="num">§ 06 - trust model</span>
      <h2>Security by design. Same binary. Two postures.</h2>
    </div>

    <div style="border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-loom-wood) 50%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lc-loom-wood) 7%, transparent); border-radius: var(--lc-radius); padding: var(--lc-space-3) var(--lc-space-4); margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-4);">
      <h3 style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);">Security by design - the substrate makes three guarantees about secrets:</h3>
      <ol style="margin: 0; padding-left: var(--lc-space-3);">
        <li style="margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);"><strong>Per-run credentials never reach the LLM.</strong> Resolved tokens are substituted at the MCP transport boundary <em>inside the runtime</em>; agents see credential <em>names</em>, never <em>values</em>. The LLM's view of its credentials map is empty of resolved tokens. Persisted state sees redacted placeholders.</li>
        <li style="margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-2);"><strong>Outbound scrub before the model sees data.</strong> The <code class="inline">redact</code> plugin in the run-loop chain scrubs secrets from every outbound LLM request - <strong>Tier-A</strong>: operator-declared env-var values get masked exactly (<em>customizable</em> - add an env var to the operator secrets map, the plugin masks its value everywhere outbound); <strong>Tier-B</strong>: built-in heuristic patterns catch <code class="inline">Authorization</code> headers, <code class="inline">sk-…</code> OpenAI keys, <code class="inline">ghp_…</code> GitHub tokens, AWS / Slack / generic <code class="inline">key=value</code> shapes regardless of operator config.</li>
        <li style="margin-bottom: 0;"><strong>Value-based redaction at rest.</strong> Anything that bypasses (1) and (2) - an agent inlining a token into a Bash command, for example - is caught at persistence time. SQLite/Postgres never store the literal token; the match is value-based, so an operator's typo (assigning the token to a differently-named shell var) is caught anyway.</li>
      </ol>
      <p style="margin-top: var(--lc-space-2); margin-bottom: 0; color: var(--lc-text-muted); font-size: var(--lc-text-sm);">
        These guarantees are <em>unconditional</em> - they hold across both postures below. <strong>Postures change what tools an agent can call. The secret-isolation guarantees never change.</strong>
        <a href="/blog/scrub-before-the-model-sees-it.html" style="color: var(--lc-loom-wood); border-bottom: 1px dashed currentColor;">redact plugin writeup →</a> · <a href="/blog/three-mcp-tokens-one-run.html" style="color: var(--lc-loom-wood); border-bottom: 1px dashed currentColor;">per-run credentials writeup →</a>
      </p>
    </div>

    <p class="lede">The UNIX shape you already know - operator, caller, agent. Operator config is the floor; callers can narrow per-request but never widen. The bearer token is the authority.</p>

    <div class="trust-grid">
      <div class="trust-col deny">
        <div class="label">posture A</div>
        <h3>True managed sandbox</h3>
        <ul>
          <li>Default-deny every tool</li>
          <li>No FS roots</li>
          <li>No Bash</li>
          <li>Caller-authoritative <code>allowed_hosts</code></li>
          <li>No outbound by default</li>
        </ul>
        <p class="when">Shared-server deployments processing untrusted input. Multi-tenant SaaS. Anywhere the caller isn't the operator.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="trust-col allow">
        <div class="label">posture B</div>
        <h3>Agentic dev environment</h3>
        <ul>
          <li>Bash on, scoped FS roots</li>
          <li>Broad <code>allowed_hosts</code></li>
          <li>Local Ollama for offline work</li>
          <li>Operator-trusted tooling</li>
          <li>Iteration speed prioritized</li>
        </ul>
        <p class="when">Local development. Internal trusted operators. The single-machine workflow where you <em>are</em> the caller.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <p class="trust-footer">
      <strong>Same UNIX shape</strong> you already know - operator, caller, agent. The bearer
      token is the authority. Operator config is the floor; callers can narrow
      per-request but <strong>never widen</strong>.
    </p>

    <p class="trust-footer" style="margin-top: var(--lc-space-3);">
      <strong>The <code class="inline">contextplugin</code> chain is the v1.0 trust-extensibility surface.</strong>
      Plugins run on a <em>copy</em> of the outbound LLM request - the persisted transcript stays canonical (clean for replay; code-as-agent's stateless replay would trip on mutated bytes). The chain is built once at boot from operator config; every plugin is deterministic, idempotent, copy-on-write. First built-in is <code class="inline">redact</code>; <strong>a context-compressor plugin is the next built-in coming</strong> (moves the v0.32.0 auto-compaction logic into the plugin surface so operators can write or swap their own compaction strategy). Beyond the built-ins, operators add their own scrubbing rules without touching agent code - declare an env-var name in the operator secrets map, the existing <code class="inline">redact</code> plugin masks its value everywhere outbound. The <code class="inline">redact_tool_input</code> opt-in extends the masking to JSON tool-input fields too.
    </p>

    <p class="trust-footer" style="margin-top: var(--lc-space-3);">
      <strong>Route by data sensitivity.</strong> The common config holds a shared
      provider-resolution structure; each agent can override it per-agent - provider, tier,
      or a specific model - from its <code class="inline">.md</code> frontmatter, a static
      YAML block, or the Web UI. Pin sensitive-data agents to a <strong>local model</strong>
      (<code class="inline">ollama-local</code>) so their data physically never leaves your
      infrastructure; route everything else to the best cloud model for the job. Local
      where it matters, cloud where it doesn't - the operator sets the classification,
      the runtime enforces it per-agent. (Residency you can prove with a packet capture,
      not a retention promise you have to trust.)
    </p>
  </section>

  <section class="section" id="war-story">
    <div class="section-head" style="margin-bottom: var(--lc-space-3);">
      <span class="num">§ 10 - from a loop to a substrate</span>
    </div>
    <div class="war-story">
      <video class="agent-anchor mascot-video" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata" poster="assets/mascots/loom-mascot-red.poster.jpg" aria-hidden="true"><source src="assets/mascots/loom-mascot-red.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
      <div class="body">
        <h2>How loomcycle became what it is.</h2>
        <p>
          loomcycle started as the <strong>agentic-loop sidecar built for
          JobEmber.ai</strong> - an AI-driven job-search SaaS that needed a shared
          runtime for many parallel per-user agents. Each user's nightly batch
          touches three per-user MCP servers (jobs API, Slack, Telegram), runs
          on a cron schedule, and reaches them with per-user bearers the agent
          never sees. The shape we wanted: multi-tenancy, scheduled runs,
          signed webhook ingress, OTEL spans, pause-anytime - in one Go binary
          you could run on a small VPS, not bolted onto the application that
          consumes it.
        </p>
        <p>
          Over the following months that sidecar grew into a generally-useful
          agentic runtime. The substrate primitives - Memory, Channel,
          AgentDef, Scheduler, Webhook, A2A, Evaluation, Context - emerged
          from real JobEmber.ai pain. The trust model came from the day a
          reviewer agent inlined a Gitea token into a Bash command and the
          runtime had to catch it. The 8-hour stability soak came from a
          production-load question: would this thing survive a long night? It
          did - <strong>1.27M circuits, 3.8M agent runs, 100% completion
          across 468 waves, zero leaks</strong>.
        </p>
        <p>
          JobEmber.ai is still its first consumer. loomcycle is now Apache-2.0,
          available to anyone with the same shape of problem - and a sidecar
          shape that integrates cleanly when Claude Code is your operator and
          conversation surface. The runtime is <strong>around 50 MB resident</strong>;
          one Go binary, no subprocess in the hot path.
        </p>
        <div class="punch">
          <p style="margin: 0;">
            Substrate primitives emerge from production pain, not whiteboards.
            <strong>JobEmber.ai's first; everyone else's next.</strong>
          </p>
        </div>
        <a href="https://github.com/denn-gubsky/loomcycle/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md" class="read-more">
          Read the architecture →
        </a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  // Pause mascot/hero videos when scrolled off-screen, resume when back in view -
  // keeps the CPU/battery cost bounded while a visitor reads sections lower on the page.
  // No-op if IntersectionObserver isn't available (very old browsers; the videos just play continuously).
  if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
      for (const e of entries) {
        const v = e.target;
        if (e.isIntersecting) { v.play().catch(() => {}); }
        else { v.pause(); }
      }
    }, { rootMargin: '50px' });
    document.querySelectorAll('video.mascot-video, video.hero-logo').forEach((v) => observer.observe(v));
  }

  // Hero video: cycle through the clips listed in data-hero-loop, then loop back to the first.
  document.querySelectorAll('video[data-hero-loop]').forEach((v) => {
    let clips;
    try { clips = JSON.parse(v.dataset.heroLoop); } catch (_) { return; }
    if (!Array.isArray(clips) || clips.length === 0) return;
    let i = 0;
    v.addEventListener('ended', () => {
      i = (i + 1) % clips.length;
      v.src = clips[i];
      v.load();
      v.play().catch(() => {});
    });
  });
